To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cancer survivors with more somatic symptoms report greater stress and this association is partially explained by fear of recurrence or disease progression.
cancer survivors’ fear of recurrence or disease progression is a mechanism through which somatic symptom severity is associated with perceived stress.
somatic symptoms are related to stress in cancer survivors and this relationship is partially mediated by fear of recurrence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the psychological and physical health of cancer survivors
the relationship between stress and physical health in cancer survivors and the role that fear of recurrence or cancer progression might play as an intermediary.
the impact of cancer-related somatic symptoms on stress and quality of life in cancer survivors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fear of recurrence and/or progression is the main cause of stress among cancer survivors and the main reason for the high prevalence of somatic symptoms in this group of patients.
the fear of recurrence or disease progression is an intermediary in the relationship between somatic symptoms severity and perceived stress in a heterogeneous sample of cancer survivors.
fear of recurrence or progress is a mechanism that can be used to explain the relationship between somatic symptoms severity and perceived stress in cancer survivors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
fear of recurrence or progressions is a mediator between somatic symptom and stress in cancer survivors.
fear of recurrence is a mechanism by which somatic symptoms contribute to stress in cancer survivors.
fear of recurrence or fear of progression may be a mediator between the presence of somatic symptoms and stress.
The main takeaway from our work is that
somatic symptoms are a source of stress for cancer survivors and that fear of recurrence or progressions may be one mechanism that links the two.
cancer survivors’ somatic symptoms can lead to increased stress and anxiety about cancer recurrence or progression, which may in turn affect the quality of their life.
fear of recurrence or disease progression may be a mechanism underlying somatic symptom severity in survivors.
